questions.text: A computer built with integrated circuits but before the invention of the microprocessor belongs to which generation of computers?
questions.explanation: The third generation (1964–1971) used integrated circuits. The first used vacuum tubes, the second transistors, and the fourth microprocessors.

questions.text: Ada Lovelace is credited as the first programmer for her work on the notes describing
questions.explanation: Lovelace wrote notes on Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine, including an algorithm for computing Bernoulli numbers, making her the first programmer.

questions.text: Which class of computer is designed to serve many users at the same time and to handle very large databases for an organisation?
questions.explanation: Mainframes support hundreds of simultaneous users and huge transaction volumes. Microcomputers serve one user, workstations serve technical single users, and embedded systems control single devices.

questions.text: The first commercially available general-purpose electronic computer was the
questions.explanation: UNIVAC I (1951) was the first computer sold commercially. ENIAC was earlier but built for the US Army, while EDVAC and EDSAC were experimental stored-program machines.

questions.text: The abacus is best described as
questions.explanation: The abacus is a manual bead device used for counting and arithmetic for centuries, long before electronic computing.

questions.text: Vacuum tubes were the main electronic component of computers of the
questions.explanation: First-generation computers (1940s–1950s) used vacuum tubes. The second generation used transistors, the third integrated circuits, and the fourth microprocessors.

questions.text: Convert 45₁₀ to binary.
How many distinct values can be represented using 8 bits?
questions.explanation: With 8 bits there are 2⁸ = 256 possible combinations, from 00000000 to 11111111. 255 is the largest unsigned value, not the count of values.

questions.text: Convert 2F₁₆ to decimal.
questions.explanation: 2F₁₆ = 2 × 16 + 15 = 32 + 15 = 47. F in hexadecimal equals 15 in decimal.

questions.text: In 8-bit two's complement notation, the representation of −5 is
questions.explanation: 5 is 00000101; inverting the bits gives 11111010 and adding 1 gives 11111011, the two's complement form of −5.

questions.text: One megabyte of storage is equal to
questions.explanation: In the binary convention used for memory, 1 MB = 1024 KB = 1,048,576 bytes.

questions.text: Convert 11010₂ to octal.
questions.explanation: Grouping the bits in threes from the right: 011 010 = 3 2, so 11010₂ = 32₈.

questions.text: Which register holds the memory address of the next instruction to be fetched for execution?
questions.explanation: The program counter keeps the address of the next instruction. The accumulator holds data being processed, while the MAR holds the address of the location being accessed.

questions.text: Which printer type produces output by striking an inked ribbon against paper?
questions.explanation: Dot-matrix printers are impact printers: pins strike a ribbon. Inkjet printers spray ink, laser printers use toner and heat, and thermal printers use heat-sensitive paper.

questions.text: A computer loses unsaved work during a power cut because the work was held in
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile, so its contents vanish when power fails. Hard disks, ROM and flash drives are non-volatile and retain data without power.

questions.text: The component of the CPU that carries out arithmetic calculations and logical comparisons is the
questions.explanation: The ALU performs arithmetic and logic. The control unit fetches and decodes instructions, registers hold data temporarily, and cache is fast memory.

questions.text: Which storage device has no moving parts and stores data in flash memory chips?
questions.explanation: An SSD uses flash memory with no moving parts, making it faster and more shock-resistant than a hard disk, tape or optical disc.

questions.text: Which bus carries memory addresses from the CPU to memory?
questions.explanation: The address bus carries the location being accessed. The data bus carries the data itself and the control bus carries control signals.

questions.text: The operating system function that decides which process runs next on the CPU is known as
questions.explanation: Process scheduling allocates CPU time among competing processes. Spooling queues print jobs, paging is a memory-management technique, and defragmentation reorganises disk files.

questions.text: Utility programs such as disk defragmenters and antivirus programs are classified as
questions.explanation: System software manages and maintains the computer itself. Application software serves end-user tasks, while shareware describes a licensing model, not a software class.

questions.text: Which input device is used to read pencil marks on multiple-choice answer sheets?
questions.explanation: OMR detects marks in fixed positions on forms. OCR reads printed characters, MICR reads magnetic ink on cheques, and barcode readers read bar patterns.

questions.text: The resolution of a printer, which determines the sharpness of its output, is measured in
questions.explanation: Dots per inch (dpi) measures print resolution. Pages per minute measures speed, bits per second measures data rate, and hertz measures frequency.

questions.text: Which of the following operating systems is open-source software?
questions.explanation: Linux source code is freely available and modifiable. Windows, macOS and iOS are proprietary operating systems.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of utility software?
questions.explanation: An antivirus program maintains the system, so it is a utility. Word processors, browsers and media players are application software.

questions.text: In a spreadsheet, the formula =SUM(B2:B6) in cell B8 is copied to cell C8. The formula in C8 becomes
questions.explanation: Cell references are relative by default, so copying one column to the right shifts the column letters from B to C while the row numbers stay the same.

questions.text: In a relational database, the field that uniquely identifies each record in a table is the
questions.explanation: A primary key value is unique for every record. A foreign key links tables, a query retrieves data, and a form is an input interface.

questions.text: In word processing, the feature that combines a standard letter with a list of names and addresses to produce personalised letters is
questions.explanation: Mail merge joins a main document to a data source. A macro automates steps, a template is a reusable document format, and a hyperlink jumps to another location.

questions.text: In a spreadsheet, an absolute cell reference to cell A1 is written as
questions.explanation: Dollar signs fix both the column and the row, so $A$1 does not change when the formula is copied. A1 is relative and A$1 fixes only the row.

questions.text: In the email address ada@example.com, the part 'example.com' is the
questions.explanation: An email address has the form username@domain. 'ada' is the user name and 'example.com' identifies the mail domain.

questions.text: An IPv4 address is made up of how many bits?
questions.explanation: IPv4 addresses are 32-bit numbers, written as four decimal octets. IPv6 addresses are 128 bits.

questions.text: In which network topology is every workstation connected to a central device, so that the failure of one cable affects only one workstation?
questions.explanation: In a star, each node has its own cable to a central switch or hub. In a bus or ring, a single cable fault can disrupt the whole network.

questions.text: Which protocol is used to transfer web pages from a web server to a browser?
questions.explanation: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) carries web pages. SMTP sends mail, POP3 retrieves mail, and FTP transfers files.

questions.text: Which device forwards data packets between different networks using IP addresses?
questions.explanation: A router selects routes between networks using IP addresses. Switches and hubs operate within one network, and a repeater only regenerates signals.

questions.text: Which type of network covers a city or a metropolitan area, larger than a LAN but smaller than a WAN?
questions.explanation: A MAN spans a city, e.g. a cable TV or city-wide network. A LAN covers one building, a WAN spans countries, and a PAN covers a few metres around a person.

questions.text: The first step in solving a problem with a computer is to
options: understand and define the problem clearly
questions.explanation: A problem must be understood and defined before an algorithm, flowchart or program can be designed correctly.

questions.text: A syntax error in a program is
options: a violation of the grammar rules of the programming language
a crash caused by invalid data at run time
a failure of the computer hardware
an error in the logic of the algorithm
questions.explanation: Syntax errors break language rules, e.g. a missing bracket, and are caught by the compiler. Logic errors produce wrong results without breaking rules.

questions.text: In a flowchart, the symbol used to test a condition and branch the flow into two alternative paths is the
questions.explanation: The diamond represents a decision. The oval marks start/end, the rectangle a process, and the parallelogram input/output.

questions.text: A compiler differs from an interpreter in that a compiler
options: translates the program one line at a time
translates the entire program before execution
questions.explanation: A compiler converts the whole source program into machine code first; an interpreter translates and executes one statement at a time.

questions.text: In pseudocode, which construct repeats a block of statements for as long as a stated condition remains true?
questions.explanation: A WHILE loop is a repetition construct controlled by a condition. IF and CASE make choices, and a function call runs a named subprogram once.

questions.text: Which of the following is a low-level programming language?
questions.explanation: Assembly language uses mnemonics close to machine code. Python, Java and BASIC are high-level languages, closer to human language.

questions.text: A variable in a computer program is best described as
options: a named storage location whose value can change during execution
an error message produced by the compiler
a fixed value that never changes
questions.explanation: Variables hold values that may change while the program runs. Fixed values are constants.

questions.text: Encryption protects data by
options: compressing it to a smaller size
converting it into a form that cannot be read without the decryption key
questions.explanation: Encryption scrambles data so only holders of the key can read it. Compression reduces size but does not protect secrecy.

questions.text: A malicious program that disguises itself as legitimate software but does not replicate itself is a
questions.explanation: A Trojan horse tricks the user into running it and does not self-replicate. Worms spread on their own, viruses attach to host files, and ransomware encrypts files for payment.

questions.text: Presenting another person's work obtained from the internet as one's own, without acknowledgement, is
questions.explanation: Plagiarism is taking credit for another's work. Piracy is unauthorised copying of software, hacking is unauthorised access, and phishing is fraudulent solicitation of data.

questions.text: A firewall protects a network primarily by
options: encrypting all files on the network
controlling incoming and outgoing traffic according to security rules
questions.explanation: A firewall inspects traffic against rules and blocks what is not allowed. Encryption, antivirus scanning and backup are separate security measures.

questions.text: Software piracy refers to the
options: unauthorised copying or distribution of software
questions.explanation: Piracy is the illegal duplication or sharing of software. Virus writing, hacking and spam are different forms of computer misuse.

questions.text: Phishing attacks aim primarily to
options: trick users into revealing sensitive information
questions.explanation: Phishing uses fake messages or websites to harvest passwords and bank details. It targets people rather than hardware.

questions.text: Which service allows voice telephone calls to be made over the internet?
questions.explanation: VoIP carries voice as data packets over IP networks. FTP transfers files, SMTP sends mail, and HTTP carries web pages.

questions.text: Which data processing method collects transactions into groups and processes them together at a scheduled time?
questions.explanation: Batch processing accumulates similar transactions and runs them as a group, e.g. monthly payroll. Real-time and online processing handle each transaction immediately.

questions.text: Which backup type copies only the files that have changed since the last backup of any kind?
questions.explanation: An incremental backup copies changes since the last backup (full or incremental). A differential backup copies changes since the last full backup.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a cloud storage service?
questions.explanation: Google Drive stores files on remote servers reached over the internet. Hard disks, DVD-ROMs and flash drives are local storage devices.

questions.text: In a database table, a single row of related data is also called a
questions.explanation: A row is a record about one entity, while a column is a field. A key identifies records and a query retrieves them.

questions.text: A file path specifies
options: the location of a file within the directory structure
the size of a file in bytes
the date a file was created
questions.explanation: A path lists the folders leading to a file, e.g. C:\Users\Ada\report.docx. Size, author and date are file properties, not the path.

questions.text: The term 'digital divide' refers to
options: the gap between those who have access to digital technology and those who do not
questions.explanation: The digital divide describes unequal access to computers, the internet and digital skills between groups or regions.

questions.text: An artificial intelligence system that uses a knowledge base and inference rules to emulate the decision-making of a human expert is called
questions.explanation: Expert systems store human expertise as rules and facts and reason with them. Neural networks learn patterns from data, while robotics controllers drive physical machines.

questions.text: The output of an AND gate is 1 only when
options: any one of its inputs is 1
questions.explanation: AND gives 1 only if every input is 1. OR gives 1 if any input is 1, and XOR gives 1 when inputs differ.

questions.text: The main purpose of an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) is to
options: provide temporary power during a mains failure
remove dust from the system unit
increase the processing speed of the CPU
cool the processor during heavy use
questions.explanation: A UPS keeps the computer running briefly after a power cut so work can be saved and the system shut down safely. It does not speed up or cool the machine.

questions.text: In a robot, the device that converts electrical signals into physical movement is called an
questions.explanation: Actuators such as motors produce motion. Sensors detect conditions, the controller decides actions, and a transducer converts one form of energy to another.

questions.text: Machine learning is best described as a system that
options: improves its performance from data without being explicitly programmed for every case
assembles cars on a factory line
questions.explanation: Machine learning algorithms find patterns in data and improve with experience, rather than following only fixed, pre-written rules.

questions.text: Verification of data differs from validation in that verification
options: checks that data falls within an acceptable range
checks that data is of the correct type
checks that compulsory fields have been filled
confirms that data has been entered accurately, for example by double entry
questions.explanation: Verification checks transcription accuracy, e.g. entering data twice and comparing. Range, type and presence checks are validation checks on reasonableness.
